data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims the panel must 'show transfer to reordered or rephrased checklists that the panelists have not seen' to establish genuine reliability gain. But the problem explicitly asks for evidence 'within a single evaluation,' and a transfer test requires a second evaluation with newly constructed/reordered materials the panel has not encountered. The target thus makes the discriminator impossible to obtain under the problem's scope. Worse, SRC_001's own countercondition (reordering degrades performance even for understanding panelists because earlier items provide context for later ones) concedes that reordering is not an understanding-preserving manipulation — which means the stated biconditional ('genuine if and only if ... transfer to reordered checklists') is not a valid single-evaluation test and may be false even when the panel genuinely understands the items.
